sector_verification_note: The most heavily Tier A sector in the taxonomy — the mirror image of Sector 1, where nothing is licensed. 18 of 20 professions name a statutory licensing body. Two verified facts shape everything: NEET applies equally to government, private AND deemed colleges, so there is NO private bypass for medicine; and the NCAHP Act 2021 moved allied health from unregulated to statutorily licensed, making physiotherapy, optometry, MLT and the imaging and OT technologist roles Tier A rather than open-market.

nuances.statement: Cost is BIMODAL, not a range. A government seat costs roughly 1-5 lakh for the whole degree; a private or deemed seat costs 60 lakh to 1.2 crore. The figure shown is a blend and describes almost nobody. Which side of that line a student lands on is decided entirely by their NEET rank.
There is NO private bypass. Unlike engineering, money cannot open a door NEET has closed — the same eligibility applies to government, private and deemed colleges alike.

Null because NEET has no upper age limit and no cap on attempts. A commerce graduate is not permanently blocked — they can add PCB through NIOS and sit NEET at any age. It is a long cost, roughly 8 years, not a closed door.

The stored figure is a blend of two costs that are twenty times apart and it describes almost no real student. A government MBBS seat costs roughly 10,000-50,000 rupees a year - under 3 lakh for the whole degree, and as little as 6,000 a year at AIIMS Delhi. A private or deemed seat runs 15-25 lakh a year, 85 lakh to 1.3 crore for the course. Which one a student pays is decided entirely by their NEET rank, not by anything they can plan for.

economics.distribution is 'bimodal', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. Both pay AND cost are bimodal. A government MBBS seat costs roughly 1-5 lakh and a private or deemed seat 60 lakh to 1.2 crore; employed hospital pay and private practice income are likewise two distributions. The midpoint describes almost nobody. This is the sector-wide question DECISIONS.md has carried open since Sector 4 was built. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it.

Pay in this profession is bimodal and the stored band is a blend of the two. A government post sits on the 7th CPC matrix - AIIMS recruits Senior Nursing Officer / Staff Nurse Grade-I at Level 8, basic 47,600 to 1,51,100 rupees a month, before dearness and house rent allowance. A private hospital pays a fraction of that for the same work, and aggregate 'average salary' figures are dominated by private employment, which is why they read low. Which side a student lands on is decided by whether they clear a government recruitment examination, not by the qualification.

deviating_roles.why: Coordinators match attendants to families, handle rosters, complaints and billing for an agency. It is the step off physical care work and the only visible progression in this profession.
End-of-life care is physically and emotionally the hardest work here - pain, distress, families and death, sustained over weeks in someone's home with no clinical team present.
Living in a client's home collapses the boundary between work and life entirely. Hours are nominal, privacy is absent, and it is the arrangement most open to exploitation.

ai_exposure.reason: Almost unexposed, and the honest note is that this is one of the professions AI is most often wrongly predicted to replace. Care is lifting, washing, feeding, watching and being present with a person who is frightened or in pain. Monitoring devices and reminder systems assist the attendant; they do not do the work. Care Coordinator carries the only real exposure, through scheduling and matching software.

nuances.statement: High and structurally rising, and this is one of the most reliable demand signals in the dataset. India's population is ageing, households are smaller, and adult children increasingly live in other cities or countries. The need for paid care at home grows directly from all three and none of them reverses.

Null, and it is a serious gap. Attendants handle medication reminders, mobility, catheters and vulnerable adults with no statutory qualification, no register and no background verification requirement. The Nursing councils regulate nurses; nothing regulates this.

Built in Sector 18 and moved here on independent review. The substitution test decided it: swap the home for a hospital ward and the work - bathing, feeding, positioning, mobility, post-operative and palliative support - survives unchanged, so the SETTING is the tag and the object of concern is a dependent person's body. It also belongs beside Nurse and Emergency Medical Technician psychometrically rather than beside Beautician and Tattoo Artist. DECISIONS.md 2.06 had assigned this base layer to Sector 4 all along.

admin_review.reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian home care attendants, agency or private, and the AGENCY MARGIN - the gap between what a family pays and what the attendant receives - is reportedly large and is the single most decision-relevant number for anyone entering this work. Separately, GENERAL DUTY ASSISTANT - the hospital ward counterpart, and the other half of the base layer DECISIONS.md 2.06 assigns to this sector - still has no record anywhere and should be added beside this one.

professions.one_liner: The hospital ward attendant - moves, washes, feeds and watches patients, and assists nurses.

deviating_roles.why: Theatre attendants work inside a sterile field discipline - positioning patients, handling equipment, managing waste - where a breach has consequences nobody sees for days. It is the most technical version of this work and the usual step up.
Emergency work is unpredictable, physically heavy and frequently distressing - trauma, intoxication, families in crisis - with no control over what arrives.
Long-stay elderly care is relationship work over weeks and months rather than episodic assistance, and it is the closest ward role to home care.

Rare, and correctly so. This role exists inside a hospital's clinical hierarchy under nursing supervision - there is no independent version. Anyone offering freelance 'ward attendant' work is describing home care, which is the separate record beside this one.

Fails the compensation filter, and it is one of the largest entry-level healthcare jobs in India for a school-leaver with no degree. The distinction that actually determines pay and benefits is not the hospital's name but whether employment is DIRECT or through a manpower agency - and most of it is through an agency.

admin_review.reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian General Duty Assistants, and the direct-versus-agency employment split - which determines pay, provident fund and job security more than the employer does - is unquantified. The ANM and GNM nursing route is named as the way up and its cost and duration are not stated on this record; a student deciding whether to take a three-month GDA course or a two-year ANM programme has nothing here to compare.

NOT A PROFESSION - a set of job roles. Coding, billing and claims work is classifying documents against a published rulebook and getting a payer to pay. sector_admin_review.reason: RESEARCHED, NOT RESOLVED - the finding is that the schema cannot express the answer. Sector 4 pay is BIMODAL, the same shape as the MBBS cost problem. Government posts sit on a published statutory matrix: AIIMS places allied health at 7th CPC Levels 4 to 6 and nursing at Level 8, basic 25,500 to 1,51,100 a month before allowances. Private hospitals pay a fraction - reported at roughly a third for nurses. Commercial aggregators were checked and are unusable: PayScale, Indeed, Glassdoor and SalaryExpert disagree by four to five times on the SAME profession, and their averages are dominated by private employment. Every economics block therefore stays 'judgment' rather than being fake-verified against a source that contradicts its neighbour. The decision owed is presentational, not factual: does a profession get one blended band, or a government band and a private band? The same decision settles Doctor's cost. Nine professions now carry a nuance recording their statutory pay level.
